dedupe_keys.name: national energy efficiency data framework need great britain

description: The National Energy Efficiency Data-Framework (NEED) was set up to understand energy use and energy efficiency in domestic and non-domestic buildings in Great Britain. It is run by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, which publishes annual reports as accredited official statistics in a GOV.UK collection first published in October 2013 and last updated on 11 June 2026 with the summary of analysis for 2026. The framework matches gas and electricity consumption data, collected for the sub-national energy consumption statistics, with records of energy efficiency measures installed in homes under government schemes such as the Energy Company Obligation and the Green Homes Grant, and with property attributes and household characteristics from other sources. A separate collection covers non-domestic buildings (ND-NEED), with annual releases to 2025. Coverage: Great Britain. Access: reports and tables on GOV.UK. Licence: Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: published outputs are aggregated; record-level data were not described on the pages read. Simulation uses: energy use by dwelling type and the savings from insulation and other measures, for building stock and retrofit models. Related records: the England and Wales energy performance certificates and the Energy Follow-Up Survey.
